title: The equality locus of two finite open subschemes is open
statement:
Let $q:M\to T$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] in the universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $Z_1,Z_2\subseteq M$ be open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion] such that each restricted morphism $q_i:Z_i\to T$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Set
$$D=q_1(|Z_1|\setminus|Z_2|)\cup q_2(|Z_2|\setminus|Z_1|),\qquad V=T\setminus D.$$
Then $D$ is closed, and $V$ with its induced open subscheme structure has the following property: for every scheme morphism $h:T'\to T$,
$$h(|T'|)\subseteq |V|\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Z_1\times_TT'=Z_2\times_TT'\text{ as open subschemes of }M\times_TT'.$$
Here fibre products are those of [def-pc-fibre-product]. In particular the subfunctor of $h_T$ defined by this equality is represented by $V\hookrightarrow T$. No separatedness of $q$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 04PK (lemma-finite-diagonal), proof: construction of the open equality locus V, for scheme test objects.

proof.text: Put $C_1=|Z_1|\setminus|Z_2|$ and $C_2=|Z_2|\setminus|Z_1|$. Each $C_i$ is closed in $Z_i$, since $Z_1\cap Z_2$ is open there. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] applied to the finite map $q_i$, its image $q_i(C_i)$ is closed in $T$. Their union $D$ is closed, so $V=T\setminus D$ is open. Give $V$ the restricted structure sheaf. Each $v\in V$ has an affine open neighbourhood contained in $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]; hence this restricted locally ringed space is a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Its inclusion is an open immersion by [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 04PK (lemma-finite-diagonal), proof: construction of the open equality locus V, for scheme test objects. Closedness and the open-subscheme construction; Schemes Tags 01IK (lemma-open-subspace-scheme), 01IT (lemma-basis-affine-opens).

proof.text: Fix $h:T\!\prime\to T$ and put $P=M\times_TT\!\prime$, with projections $r:P\to M$, $s:P\to T\!\prime$. Write $Z_i\!\prime=Z_i\times_TT\!\prime$. The natural map $Z_i\!\prime\to P$ is the base change of $Z_i\hookrightarrow M$ along $r$: a test pair $a:W\to Z_i$, $b:W\to P$ with $j_i a=rb$ gives the unique map to $Z_i\!\prime$ from $(a,sb)$, and its map to $P$ is $b$ because both projections agree. This verifies the pullback property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] makes $Z_i\!\prime$ an open subscheme of $P$. The image clause of [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image] on this square identifies its underlying open with $r^{-1}(|Z_i|)$.

source.place: Tag 04PK (lemma-finite-diagonal), proof: construction of the open equality locus V, for scheme test objects. Base-changed opens; Schemes Tag 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion), Morphisms Tag 01S1 (lemma-base-change-surjective), proof.

proof.text: By Step 2 the symmetric difference of the two underlying opens in $P$ is $E=r^{-1}(C_1)\cup r^{-1}(C_2)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image] to the defining square $P=M\times_TT\!\prime$, separately for $C_1,C_2\subseteq|M|$. It gives $s(r^{-1}(C_i))=h^{-1}(q(C_i))$, hence $s(E)=h^{-1}(D)$. A set is empty if and only if its image under a function is empty. Consequently the two opens agree exactly when $h^{-1}(D)=\varnothing$, equivalently $h(|T\!\prime|)\subseteq V$. An open subscheme has the restricted structure sheaf [def-weil-open-immersion], so equality of its underlying open is equality as an open subscheme. This proves both directions of the asserted equivalence.

source.place: Tag 04PK (lemma-finite-diagonal), proof: construction of the open equality locus V, for scheme test objects. Expansion of the final sentence that V works, using the arbitrary-subset image identity in Morphisms Tag 01S1 (lemma-base-change-surjective), proof.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme], a morphism $h:T\!\prime\to T$ has image in $V$ exactly when it has a unique factorization through $V\hookrightarrow T$. Step 3 identifies these morphisms with those for which $Z_1\!\prime=Z_2\!\prime$. Thus composition with $V\hookrightarrow T$ gives a bijection from morphisms $T\!\prime\to V$ to this equality subfunctor. These bijections commute with precomposition: the precomposed factorization is a factorization of the precomposed map and uniqueness identifies it with the chosen one. They therefore give the claimed representation. Only the restrictions $q_i$ were required finite; no separatedness of $q$ was used.

lean.statement: theorem finite_open_equality_locus {M T : Scheme.{u}} (q : M ⟶ T) (Z₁ Z₂ : M.Opens) [IsFinite (Z₁.ι ≫ q)] [IsFinite (Z₂.ι ≫ q)] : IsClosed (q '' ((Z₁ : Set M) \ (Z₂ : Set M)) ∪ q '' ((Z₂ : Set M) \ (Z₁ : Set M))) ∧ ∃ V : T.Opens, (V : Set T) = (q '' ((Z₁ : Set M) \ (Z₂ : Set M)) ∪ q '' ((Z₂ : Set M) \ (Z₁ : Set M)))ᶜ ∧ (∀ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (h : T' ⟶ T), Set.range h ⊆ (V : Set T) ↔ (pullback.fst q h) ⁻¹ᵁ Z₁ = (pullback.fst q h) ⁻¹ᵁ Z₂) ∧ (∀ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (h : T' ⟶ T), (pullback.fst q h) ⁻¹ᵁ Z₁ = (pullback.fst q h) ⁻¹ᵁ Z₂ ↔ ∃! k : T' ⟶ V.toScheme, k ≫ V.ι = h)
